requirements.text: Web location dialog shall be accessed from the menubar and keyboard.
It shall be possible to open a web location (URL) in the current Navigator window (including the dismiss dialog).
It shall be possible to open a web location (URL) in a new Navigator window (including the dismiss dialog).
It shall be possible to open web location in a Composer window (including the dismiss dialog).
Error shall be displayed while trying to open a nonexistent (bogus) web location.
It shall be possible to open local files (both HTML and plain text tested) in the current Navigator window (including the dismiss dialog).
It shall be possible to open local files (both HTML and plain text tested) in a new Navigator window (including the dismiss dialog).
ıt shall be possible to open local files (both HTML and plain text tested) in a Composer window (including the dismiss dialog).
Error shall be displayed while trying to open a nonexistent (bogus) local file.

reference_cases.title: TC-166
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
The browser should already be open.

STEPS/DESCRIPTION
Test the following to see if all of these tasks will bring up the Open Web Location dialog:
1. From the menubar of the browser, select File > Open Web Location.
2. Use the keyboard shortcut specific to your platform: 
Win32 and Unix: Control+Shift+L
Macintosh: Command+Shift+L

EXPECTED RESULTS
The Open Web Location should be displayed, regardless of the means you used above.

reference_cases.title: TC-167
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
The Open Web Location dialog should already be opened in the browser.

STEPS/DESCRIPTION - I
1. In the textfield enter the URL http://www.mozillazine.org/.
2. Select Current Navigator window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
3. Click the Open button (or hit Enter).

EXPECTED RESULTS -I
The dialog should go away and the URL load into the current browser window.


STEPS/DESCRIPTION - II
1. In the textfield enter the URL http://www.mozillazine.org/.
2. Select Current Navigator window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
3. Click the Cancel button (or hit Esc).

EXPECTED RESULTS -II
The dialog should go away and the page in the current browser window remain unchanged.

reference_cases.title: TC-169
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
The Open Web Location dialog should already be opened in the browser.

STEPS/DESCRIPTION - UI Test
1. In the textfield enter the URL http://www.mozilla.org/quality/browser/front-end/testcases/xpapps-gui/open-URL/files/boring.html.
2. Select New Composer window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
3. Click the Open button (or hit Enter).

2. An editor window should appear.
3. The page contents of the URL should load into the editor window.

2. Select New Composer window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
3. Click the Cancel button (or hit Esc).

EXPECTED RESULTS - Dismissal test
The dialog should go away and the page in the current browser window remain unchanged.

reference_cases.title: TC-170
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
The Open Web Location dialog should already be opened in the browser.

STEPS/DESCRIPTION
1. In the textfield enter the URL http://www.mozilla.org/lizard-eats-all/blarg.html.
2. Select Current Navigator window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
3. Click the Open button (or hit Enter).

EXPECTED RESULTS
1. The dialog should go away.
2. Since this page doesn't exist (well, it shouldn't ;-), the page that loads should display the typical 404 error: 
Not Found: The requested object does not exist on this server. The link you followed is either outdated, inaccurate, or the server has been instructed not to let you have it.

reference_cases.title: TC-171
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
1. Copy boring.html and dull.txt into a folder on your machine (eg, your desktop).
2. Then bring up the Open Web Location dialog in the browser.
 
STEPS/DESCRIPTION - UI test #1
1. Click the Choose File... button.
2. In the resulting file picker dialog, navigate and select the boring.html file.
3. Click Open in the file picker to dismiss it.
4. Select Current Navigator window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
5. Click the Open button (or hit Enter).

EXPECTED RESULTS - UI test #1
1. After step #3, the full path and filename should be displayed in the textfield of the Open Web Location dialog.
2. After the last step, the Open Web Location dialog should be dismissed, and boring.html displayed in the current browser window.


STEPS/DESCRIPTION - Dismissal #1 
1. Click the Choose File... button.
2. In the resulting file picker dialog, navigate and select the boring.html file.
3. Click Open in the file picker to dismiss it.
4. Select Current Navigator window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
5. Click the Cancel button (or hit Esc).

EXPECTED RESULTS - Dismissal #1 
The dialog should go away and the page in the current browser window remain unchanged.
 
STEPS/DESCRIPTION - UI test #2
1. Click the Choose File... button.
2. In the resulting file picker dialog, navigate and select the dull.txt file.

4. Select Current Navigator window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
5. Click the Open button (or hit Enter).

1. After step #3, the full path and filename should be displayed in the textfield of the Open Web Location dialog.
2. After the last step, the Open Web Location dialog should be dismissed, and dull.txt displayed in the current browser window.


STEPS/DESCRIPTION - Dismissal #2

2. In the resulting file picker dialog, navigate and select the dull.txt file.
3. Click Open in the file picker to dismiss it.
4. Select Current Navigator window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
5. Click the Cancel button (or hit Esc).

reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
The Open Web Location dialog should already be opened in the browser.

STEPS/DESCRIPTION
1. Click the Choose File... button.
2. In the resulting file picker dialog, enter the filename of a file which doesn't exist locally on your machine, eg, 
Navigate to your desktop location, or stay at whatever directory the file picker is currently at.
Enter fibble-diddle-teehee.html.
5. Click Open in the file picker to dismiss it.
6. Select Current Navigator window from the droplist, if it isn't already displayed there.
7. Click the Open button (or hit Enter).

EXPECTED RESULTS

technique_rationales.equivalence_partitioning: Required to test valid input partitions such as real URLs and existing local HTML/plain text files, alongside invalid input partitions such as nonexistent URLs and bogus local files.
technique_rationales.state_transition: Required to test opening and dismissing the web location dialog across different window contexts like the current Navigator window, new Navigator window, and Composer window.
technique_rationales.use_case: Required to cover end-to-end user workflows starting from accessing the web location dialog via menubar or keyboard to opening targets in various windows and dismissing the dialog.
technique_rationales.error_guessing: Required to explore plausible failure conditions such as submitting nonexistent or bogus web locations and local files to verify error display requirements.
